title: GRASP responsibility patterns
idea: GRASP (General Responsibility Assignment Software Patterns) is nine guidelines for choosing which class owns each job; Low Coupling and High Cohesion are two of them.
points: Information Expert: give a job to the class holding the data it needs.
Creator: a class creates objects it contains or closely uses.
Controller: one object receives a system event and delegates the work.
Pure Fabrication invents a helper; Indirection puts it between callers and a varying part.

hero.title: Who does what in an order

edges.label: addItem
edges.caption: The route hands the system event to a controller, keeping business rules out of the UI.

edges.label: addLine
edges.caption: The controller delegates. It decides nothing about prices itself.

edges.label: new
edges.caption: `Order` contains lines, so it is the Creator of each `LineItem`.

edges.label: subtotal
edges.caption: Each line knows price and quantity, so it is the Expert for its subtotal.

edges.label: taxFor
edges.caption: `TaxService` is invented, not a domain noun: a Pure Fabrication that keeps `Order` cohesive.

edges.label: calc
edges.caption: Rules share one `calc` shape. New regions add a class: Protected Variations through Polymorphism.

code.title: Expert, Creator, Controller
code.caption: Add a `discount` to `LineItem.subtotal`. Only the Expert changes.

walk.text: `LineItem` holds price and quantity, so it computes its own subtotal.
`Order` aggregates lines, so it creates them.
`Order` is the Expert for the total: it asks each line.
The controller receives events and delegates; no pricing logic lives here.
Two events, then read the total.

code.title: Fabrication and variation
code.caption: Add a `HalfTax` rule for a new region. `TaxService` stays the same.

pitfalls: Do not let one controller grow business rules; it should only delegate.
Avoid fabricating helpers for data a domain class already owns.
Protect only points likely to vary; every extra layer costs reading time.

quiz.q: An `Invoice` holds its lines and their prices. Which class should compute the invoice total?
options: The controller that handles the request
The repository that loads the invoice
quiz.why: Information Expert: `Invoice` already has the lines and prices, so computing there needs no extra coupling.

takeaway: Give each job to the class that already knows enough to do it.
